take: Developers complain on X every day about their tools, their cloud bills and the job market, but nobody adds it up. The Developer Pain Index turns those posts into a monthly report you can cite, with every chart showing its sample size and dates.

Developers complain on X every day about their tools, their cloud bills and the job market, but nobody adds it up. The Developer Pain Index turns those posts into a monthly report you can cite, with every chart showing its sample size and dates.

Each month, Grok from xAI searches X for complaint posts in each category, and rates how severe each one is. Everything after that runs on Modal, which groups the complaints into themes, saves the dataset to a Volume and serves the report page.

Each month, Grok from ex A I searches X for complaint posts in each category, and rates how severe each one is. Everything after that runs on Modal, which groups the complaints into themes, saves the dataset to a Volume and serves the report page.

Why Modal? This job runs once a month, so a laptop script would have to stay awake for it, and your own server would sit idle the rest of the time. Modal starts the pull on a cron schedule and keeps the xAI key in a Secret. A Volume stores the results, and a web endpoint serves the page at a public URL. Between runs it scales to zero, so you only pay for the seconds it works.

Why Modal? This job runs once a month, so a laptop script would have to stay awake for it, and your own server would sit idle the rest of the time. Between runs it scales to zero, so you only pay for the seconds it works.
When it runs, one .map() call spreads the searches across containers, so the six-month backfill ran 30 searches in parallel and kept 704 posts.
When it runs, one dot map call spreads the searches across containers, so the six month backfill ran thirty searches in parallel and kept seven hundred and four posts.
